verdict.rationale: Gusto ships a per-endpoint API reference (reference pages for webhook subscriptions, time-off decline, health checks and more) and publishes Postman collections for each API version, which give runnable request examples. The evidence never shows that the reference itself is interactive (no in-page 'try it' console), and runnable execution depends on an external Postman client. Missing for 10: evidence of an in-browser interactive/try-it console in the reference, documented runnable code samples per endpoint, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: We publish separate collections for each API version.
Create a webhook subscription to receive events of the specified subscription_types whenever there is a state change.
